questions.question: What is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults?
questions.detail: Myxomas are the most common primary benign cardiac tumor in adults.

questions.question: What is the most common location for a cardiac myxoma?
choices: Left atrium, attached to the fossa ovalis
questions.detail: About 75% occur in the left atrium, often attached to the interatrial septum by a stalk.

questions.question: The most common primary MALIGNANT cardiac tumor in adults is:
questions.detail: Angiosarcomas are aggressive and characteristically involve the right atrium.

questions.question: A cardiac mass that is "T1 hyperintense" and "nulls" on fat-saturation sequences is a:
questions.detail: These follow fat signal on all MRI sequences.

questions.question: "Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum" is a benign condition that classically SPARES which region?
questions.detail: The "dumbbell" shape occurs because the fat accumulation spares the fossa ovalis.

questions.question: On CMR, how can you best differentiate a cardiac THROMBUS from a tumor?
choices: Thrombus will NOT enhance on first-pass perfusion or LGE
Tumor is always in the RA
questions.detail: Because thrombus is avascular, it does not take up gadolinium (except for very old, organized clots which may show peripheral enhancement).

questions.question: Primary cardiac lymphoma most commonly involves which part of the heart?
choices: Right side of the heart (RA and RV)
questions.detail: Lymphoma is rare but favors the right heart and can present with pericardial effusions.

questions.question: Metastatic disease to the heart is much more common than primary tumors. Which malignancy is most likely to involve the heart?
questions.detail: Melanoma has the highest rate of cardiac involvement per case, while lung/breast are common due to sheer prevalence.

questions.question: A cardiac mass with a "sunburst" appearance on CT due to its vascularity and central necrosis is most likely an:
questions.detail: These are highly vascular, invasive masses in the RA.

questions.question: Papillary fibroelastomas are small, benign tumors most commonly found on:
choices: Heart valves (especially the Aortic or Mitral valves)
questions.detail: They are small, "frond-like" tumors that attach to the valves and can embolize.
